source.title: Benchmarking Neural Decoding Backbones towards Enhanced On-edge iBCI Applications
source.authors: Zhou Zhou; Guo-Hang He; Zheng Zhang; L. Leng; Qinghai Guo; Jian-Xing Liao; Xuan Song; Ran Cheng

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling by model size in neural decoding, a setting beyond language-model pretraining, and reports model-specific results.
record.gate_note: The paper varies model size for neural-decoding backbones and reports R² outcomes, so those results are recorded below. It does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy, vary training tokens or compute, test compute-optimal allocations, or fit and report power-law exponents. Results from the single-session, multi-session and fine-tuning experiments, and cited scaling-law findings from other work, are not rows for the versions at issue.
record.test_reason: The study scales GRU, RWKV and Mamba neural-decoding models from about 300k to about 3M parameters and reports held-out R². This is a non-text setting, so it bears weakly on V5. It fits no power law, covers only about one order of magnitude, and measures R² rather than loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Correction: in Table 2 and Section 5.1 Mamba reaches the highest scaled R² (0.851), RWKV reaches 0.843, and GRU reaches 0.846 before declining. The authors say RWKV and Mamba 'comply with the scaling law' only in the loose sense of improving with size; they fit no power law.
record.recipe_differences: Applies parameter scaling to neural-decoding models and evaluates R², rather than language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens or compute. No power-law fit is reported.
record.method_sensitivity: The scaling outcome differs by backbone; the authors report GRU's gains are mild and decline with further scaling, while RWKV and Mamba gains level off. The text gives inconsistent upper parameter-range descriptions (3M versus 3.8M).
record.problems: Only one dataset and one subject are used; the authors identify dataset size as a reason gains level off. The scaling result is not fitted to a power law, and no numeric uncertainty values are stated. The reported parameter range and Mamba maximum R² are inconsistent across sections.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling rows were left out. The Transformer is excluded from scaling because the paper says it can fail to converge. Other experiment results do not test the listed versions.

untested.parts: Whether the power-law functional form holds: no fit or exponent is reported. Loss as the measure (R² is used instead). Scaling in data or compute. Scaling over several orders of magnitude (only about 10x in parameters). Image/video, repeated data, and fine-tuning/transfer scaling.

missing.what: The abstract claims RWKV and Mamba improve 'with larger data sets', but no data-scaling experiment or result is reported anywhere. The record should note this as an unsupported claim, not a row.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence on V5 is very weak: a single dataset and subject, about one decade of parameters, a bounded R² metric, scaling by layer count only, the Transformer excluded, and no uncertainty values stated. The parameter range is given as 3M in the text and 3.8M in the Figure 2 caption.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model loss as a function of parameters, tokens or compute.
Whether fits from smaller runs predict much larger language-model runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations or their growth with compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
The study reports neural-decoding R² changes with parameter count, but does not fit or test a power-law form; it does not test image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer.
Downstream-task performance in language models as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations on fitting choices, and bending away from a fitted power law.
